title: India AI Governance Guidelines
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

timeline.event: Subcommittee on AI governance constituted under PSA-chaired Advisory Group
Report on AI Governance Guidelines Development released for comment
Extended comment deadline closes; 2,500+ submissions
Drafting committee chaired by Prof. Balaraman Ravindran constituted by MeitY
Final guidelines released
AIGEG constituted as the coordinating body recommended by the guidelines

summary: Voluntary framework setting principles, recommendations and an action plan for AI governance across sectors; relies on existing laws, voluntary measures and techno-legal tools rather than a new AI statute.
key_provisions: Seven sutras adapted from RBI's FREE-AI report: Trust is the Foundation; People First; Innovation over Restraint; Fairness & Equity; Accountability; Understandable by Design; Safety, Resilience & Sustainability
Six pillars: Infrastructure, Capacity Building, Policy & Regulation, Risk Mitigation, Accountability (graded liability), Institutions
States that 'at this stage, a separate law to regulate AI is not needed'; recommends targeted amendments to the IT Act and copyright law to enable large-scale AI training
Recommends an AI Governance Group (suggested chair: Principal Scientific Adviser), a Technology & Policy Expert Committee, and a resourced AI Safety Institute operating hub-and-spoke

Action plan: short term establish AIGG/TPEC, India-specific risk classification, voluntary frameworks, master circular, groundwork for AI incidents database; medium term amend laws, operationalise incident reporting, sandboxes; long term draft new laws if needed
Industry expectations: comply with Indian law, adopt voluntary frameworks, publish transparency reports, provide grievance redressal, use techno-legal mitigations
confidence_note: Full text read from the PIB-hosted PDF of the guidelines. Drafting committee month (July 2025) from the document's executive summary.

summary: Consultation draft analysing gaps in India's AI governance and recommending a whole-of-government, techno-legal approach; it preceded the November 2025 guidelines.
key_provisions: Recommended a whole-of-government approach with an Inter-Ministerial AI Coordination Committee / Governance Group
Proposed a Technical Secretariat housed in MeitY to support the committee
Proposed a national AI incident database, not to be used as an enforcement tool
Proposed voluntary transparency commitments by AI developers and deployers
Adopted a lifecycle and ecosystem view of AI actors and recommended gap analysis of existing law on deepfakes, cybersecurity and IP
Listed eight principles including transparency, accountability, safety/reliability/robustness, privacy/security, fairness, human-centred values, inclusive innovation and digital-by-design governance

title: MeitY advisory on deployment of under-testing AI models (1 March 2024)
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

timeline.event: Advisory issued; 15-day action-taken report sought
Minister clarifies advisory aimed at large platforms, not startups

summary: Advisory requiring intermediaries to seek explicit government permission before deploying under-testing or unreliable AI models to Indian users and to label AI outputs; withdrawn and replaced within two weeks.
key_provisions: Under-testing or unreliable AI models/LLMs/generative AI to be made available only with explicit permission of the Government of India
Outputs to be labelled on 'possible and inherent fallibility or unreliability'; consent pop-up mechanisms
AI tools not to permit bias, discrimination or threats to electoral integrity
Metadata/unique identifiers for synthetic content to allow identification of the originator
Action-taken-cum-status report within 15 days
